artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and consider a closed rectangle $R \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with side lengths $\sqrt{3}$ and $n-1$. For any finite set $S \subset R$ of $n$ points, define the connecting length
\[
L(S) := \inf\{\mathcal{H}^1(K) : K \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \text{ is a connected set with } S \subset K\},
\]
where $\mathcal{H}^1$ denotes one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (so $L(S)$ is the length of a Steiner tree connecting $S$). Define
\[
M(n) := \sup\{L(S) : S \subset R,\ |S| = n\}.
\]
Prove or disprove that
\[
M(n) \leq \sqrt{3}\,(n-1) + o(1) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.
\]
Equivalently: is it true that any $n$ points in a $\sqrt{3} \times (n-1)$ rectangle can always be connected by a set of total length at most $\sqrt{3}(n-1) + o(1)$? (The bound is conjectured to be asymptotically attained on the configuration consisting of the points $(2i, 0)$ and $(2i+1, \sqrt{3})$.)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific worst-case Steiner connectivity bound for n points in a √3 × (n−1) rectangle. The question is posed as an open problem attributed to a suggestion of E. Paolini, and no proof or counterexample appears in available sources.
